blocks.text: Yeh chapter 9 (Acid-Base Chemistry) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har sawal 4 number ka hai (wazahat, equations, zaroorat ho to diagram), aur chapter ke numericals qadam ba qadam hal kiye gaye hain. Har sawal ka poora model jawab hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Explain how the Bronsted-Lowry concept removed the limitation of the Arrhenius theory. Using the reactions of HCl and NH₃ with water, show that water is amphoteric. (4 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke Bronsted-Lowry concept ne Arrhenius theory ki kami kaise door ki. HCl aur NH₃ ke paani se reactions se dikhayein ke paani amphoteric hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Arrhenius theory ki kami: yeh acid aur base ka reaction sirf aqueous medium mein bayan karti hai, jab ke bohat se reactions doosre solvents mein ya baghair solvent hote hain.

Bronsted-Lowry concept (1923, J.N. Bronsted aur T.M. Lowry): acid-base reactions proton-transfer (proton ki muntaqili) reactions hain. Acid woh species hai jo proton deti hai aur base woh jo proton leti hai. Is mein paani ya OH⁻ zaroori nahi, is liye yeh har solvent mein aur baghair solvent bhi lagta hai:
HCl(g) + NH₃(g) → NH₄Cl(s)
HCl proton deta hai (acid) aur NH₃ leta hai (base), halaanke OH⁻ maujood nahi.

Paani base ke tor par: HCl(g) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
HCl ka H⁺ paani ke O atom ke lone pair se jurta hai; H₂O proton leta hai (base). Pairs: HCl-Cl⁻ aur H₂O-H₃O⁺.

Paani acid ke tor par: NH₃(g) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
H₂O ka H⁺ N ke lone pair se jurta hai; H₂O proton deta hai (acid). Pairs: NH₃-NH₄⁺ aur H₂O-OH⁻.

Paani doosre reactant ke mutabiq kabhi base aur kabhi acid banta hai, is liye amphoteric (dono khaslat wala) hai.

book_ref.quote: Bronsted-Lowry pointed out that acid–base reactions can be seen as proton-transfer reactions

blocks.prompt:
2 Define conjugate acid and conjugate base. For the reactions of HNO₃, H₂SO₄ and CO₃²⁻ with water given in Table 9.1, write each equation and name the acid, base, conjugate acid and conjugate base. (4 marks)
(Conjugate acid aur conjugate base ki definition likhein. Table 9.1 mein diye gaye HNO₃, H₂SO₄ aur CO₃²⁻ ke paani se reactions likhein aur har aik mein acid, base, conjugate acid aur conjugate base batayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Conjugate acid: woh species jo Bronsted base ke acid se proton lene ke baad banti hai (maslan H₃O⁺ paani ka conjugate acid hai).
Conjugate base: woh species jo acid ke base ko proton dene par banti hai (maslan HCl se Cl⁻).

Equations:
HNO₃ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + NO₃⁻
H₂SO₄ + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + HSO₄⁻
H₂O + CO₃²⁻ ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻

Har reaction mein acid aur us ke conjugate base mein aik proton ka farq hai, aur base aur us ke conjugate acid mein bhi aik proton ka (table dekhein).

book_ref.quote: A species formed after a Bronsted base accepts a proton from the acid is called the conjugate acid.

blocks.prompt:
3 Define Lewis acids and bases. Explain the formation of acid-base adducts from (i) silver ion and ammonia (ii) boron trifluoride and fluoride ion, and show how the charge on each adduct is found. (4 marks)
(Lewis acids aur bases ki definition likhein. (i) silver ion aur ammonia (ii) boron trifluoride aur fluoride ion se acid-base adducts ka banna samjhayein, aur dikhayein ke har adduct ka charge kaise maloom hota hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Lewis concept (G.N. Lewis, 1923): acids aur bases ki pehchaan electron pair lene ya dene aur coordinate covalent bond banane ki salahiyat se hoti hai.
Lewis acid: har woh species (molecule ya ion) jo electron pair le sake.
Lewis base: har woh species (molecule ya ion) jo electron pair de sake.
Lewis acid-base reaction tab hota hai jab base acid ko electron pair deta hai; product acid-base adduct hai.

(i) Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ → [H₃N→Ag←NH₃]⁺
Dono NH₃ molecules (Lewis bases) apna lone pair musbat silver ion (Lewis acid) ko dete hain. Baayen taraf charges = +1 + 0 + 0 = +1, is liye adduct par +1 hai.

(ii) BF₃ + F⁻ → BF₄⁻
BF₃ mein boron ke valence shell mein sirf chhe electrons hain (adhoora octet), is liye yeh electron pair leta hai aur bohat achha Lewis acid hai. Fluoride ion (Lewis base) apna aik lone pair deta hai. Baayen taraf charges = 0 + (−1) = −1, is liye adduct par −1 hai.

book_ref.quote: In the following reaction, each of two ammonia molecules, Lewis bases, donates a pair of electrons

blocks.prompt:
4 What is the ionic product of water? Derive its value at 25 °C and explain how it is affected by temperature and by adding a little acid or base. (4 marks)
(Paani ka ionic product kya hai? 25 °C par is ki qeemat nikalein aur wazahat karein ke temperature aur thora acid ya base dalne se is par kya asar hota hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Self-ionization: khalis paani kamzor magar napne ke qabil conductor hai kyun ke yeh reversible tor par ionize hota hai:
H₂O(ℓ) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq); net: H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)

Derivation: Kc = [H⁺][OH⁻]/[H₂O] = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁶ mol dm⁻³
[H₂O] = 1000 g dm⁻³ ÷ 18 g mol⁻¹ = 55.5 mol dm⁻³. Paani bohat zyada hai aur bohat kam molecules ionize hote hain, is liye [H₂O] constant hai aur Kc ke saath mila di jati hai:
Kw = Kc[H₂O] = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁶ × 55.5 ≈ 25 °C par 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴
Kw ko paani ka ionic product (dissociation constant) kehte hain.

Neutral paani: [H⁺] = [OH⁻], is liye [H⁺]² = 10⁻¹⁴ aur [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³.

Temperature ka asar (Table 9.2): temperature ke saath Kw barhta hai: 0.11 × 10⁻¹⁴ (0 °C), 0.30 × 10⁻¹⁴ (10 °C), 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ (25 °C), 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ (40 °C).

Acid ya base dalna: thore acid se [H⁺] > [OH⁻]; base ke chand qatron se [OH⁻] > [H⁺]. Dono barabar nahi rehte, magar Kw wahi rehta hai, 25 °C par 10⁻¹⁴.

book_ref.quote: Constant concentration of water is taken on L.H.S. and multiplied with Kc to get another constant called Kw.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein "Kw [H₂O] = [H⁺][OH⁻]" chhapa hai. Kw mein [H₂O] pehle se shamil hai: Kw = Kc[H₂O] = [H⁺][OH⁻]. Table 9.2 ki powers bhi 10⁻¹⁴ hain, 10¹⁴ nahi.

blocks.prompt:
5 Using Table 9.2 (Kw = 0.11 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 0 °C and 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 40 °C), calculate [H⁺] and pH of pure water at 0 °C and at 40 °C. Is the water neutral at both temperatures? (4 marks)
(Table 9.2 (0 °C par Kw = 0.11 × 10⁻¹⁴ aur 40 °C par 3.00 × 10⁻¹⁴) se 0 °C aur 40 °C par khalis paani ki [H⁺] aur pH nikalein. Kya dono temperatures par paani neutral hai?)
blocks.explanation: Khalis paani mein [H⁺] = [OH⁻], is liye har temperature par [H⁺] = √Kw; phir pH = −log[H⁺].

book_ref.quote: The effect of temperature on Kw is shown in Table 9.2.

steps: Khalis paani: [H⁺] = [OH⁻], is liye Kw = [H⁺]² aur [H⁺] = √Kw
Dono temperatures par [H⁺] = [OH⁻], is liye paani neutral hai; sirf Kw (aur neutral paani ka pH) temperature se badalta hai
blocks.final_answer: 0 °C: [H⁺] = 3.3 × 10⁻⁸ mol dm⁻³, pH = 7.48; 40 °C: [H⁺] = 1.73 × 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³, pH = 6.76; dono par neutral

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Neutral ka matlab [H⁺] = [OH⁻] hai, pH = 7 sirf 25 °C par neutral hai. Garam paani ka pH 7 se kam ho sakta hai magar woh acidic nahi hota.

blocks.prompt:
6 Define pH and pOH. Why were these scales introduced? Show that pH + pOH = 14 at 25 °C and find the pH and pOH of neutral water. (4 marks)
(pH aur pOH ki definition likhein. Yeh scales kyun banaye gaye? Dikhayein ke 25 °C par pH + pOH = 14 hai aur neutral paani ka pH aur pOH nikalein.)
blocks.explanation:
Zaroorat: aqueous solutions mein H⁺ aur OH⁻ ki concentrations itni kam hoti hain ke aasani se likhi aur hisaab mein istemal nahi hoteen. 1909 mein Danish biochemist Sorenson ne pH aur pOH pesh kiye.

Definitions:
pH = −log[H⁺]
pOH = −log[OH⁻]

Taaluq: 25 °C par Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴. Dono taraf −log lene se:
−log[H⁺] + (−log[OH⁻]) = −log(10⁻¹⁴)
pH + pOH = 14

Neutral paani: [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³
pH = −log(10⁻⁷) = 7 aur pOH = −log(10⁻⁷) = 7

Range: 25 °C par pH aam tor par 0 se 14 ke darmiyan hota hai (pH < 7 acidic, pH > 7 basic, Figure 9.1), magar manfi pH aur 14 se zyada pH wale solutions bhi maloom hain.

book_ref.quote: So, the scales of pH and pOH were developed.

blocks.prompt:
7 A solution has [H⁺] = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ at 25 °C. Calculate its pH, pOH and [OH⁻] (Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴), and state whether it is acidic or basic. (4 marks)
(25 °C par aik solution mein [H⁺] = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ hai. Is ka pH, pOH aur [OH⁻] nikalein (Kw = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴), aur batayein ke acidic hai ya basic.)
blocks.explanation: pH seedha −log[H⁺] se; pOH = 14 − pH; [OH⁻] Kw/[H⁺] se.

book_ref.quote: Use the expression for Kw: Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻]

steps: pH < 7, is liye solution acidic hai

blocks.prompt:
8 The pH of a cleaning solution is 10.4 at 25 °C. Calculate its pOH, [H⁺] and [OH⁻]. (4 marks)
(25 °C par aik safai wale solution ka pH 10.4 hai. Is ka pOH, [H⁺] aur [OH⁻] nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: pOH = 14 − pH; antilog lein: [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ aur [OH⁻] = 10⁻ᵖᴼᴴ (pH se H⁺, pOH se OH⁻).

book_ref.quote: Find the concentration of H⁺ and OH⁻, Taking antilog of pH and pOH

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book ke Sample Problem 9.1 mein "[OH⁻] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ" chhapa hai, jo ghalat hai. pH ka antilog [H⁺] deta hai aur pOH ka antilog [OH⁻].

blocks.prompt:
9 What is the ionization constant Ka of an acid? Derive its expression for a weak acid HA, state its uses, and classify acids on the basis of Ka. (4 marks)
(Acid ka ionization constant Ka kya hai? Weak acid HA ke liye is ka expression nikalein, is ke istemal batayein aur Ka ki bunyaad par acids ki darja bandi karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Bohat se acids weak electrolytes hain aur 100% se bohat kam ionize hote hain. Dissociation constant Ka acid ki taqat ka miqdaari paimana hai.

Derivation: HA + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + A⁻
Kc = [H₃O⁺][A⁻] / [HA][H₂O]
Paani bohat zyada hai, is liye is ki concentration constant hai: Kc[H₂O] = [H₃O⁺][A⁻] / [HA]
Kc[H₂O] = Ka rakhein. Lehaza Ka = [H₃O⁺][A⁻] / [HA]

Istemal:
1. Agar pH (ya [H⁺]) aur acid ki shuru ki concentration maloom ho to Ka nikal sakte hain.
2. Agar HA ki shuru ki concentration aur Ka maloom ho to equilibrium par [H₃O⁺] aur [A⁻] nikal sakte hain.

Darja bandi:
Ka < 10⁻³: weak acid (maslan CH₃COOH, Ka = 1.85 × 10⁻⁵; H₂S, 1.0 × 10⁻⁷)
Ka = 1 se 10⁻³: moderately strong acid
Ka > 1: strong acid
Ka jitna bara, acid utna strong.

book_ref.quote: Suppose we have an acid HA dissolved in water,

blocks.prompt:
10 Show that the hydronium ion concentration of a weak acid HA of molar concentration C is given by [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C). State the assumption made. (4 marks)
(Dikhayein ke molar concentration C wale weak acid HA ki hydronium ion concentration [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C) hoti hai. Kiya gaya mafrooza (assumption) bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Weak acids paani mein poori tarah dissociate nahi hote, is liye [H₃O⁺] acid ki shuru ki concentration ke barabar nahi hoti; equilibrium expression istemal hota hai.

Dissociation: HA(aq) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + A⁻(aq)
Paani mein: H⁺(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq)
Is liye: HA(aq) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + A⁻(aq)

HA ki shuru ki concentration C mol dm⁻³ ho. Equilibrium par:
[H₃O⁺] = x, [A⁻] = x, [HA] = C − x

Ka = (x × x)/(C − x) = x²/(C − x)

Mafrooza: weak acid mein x C ke muqable mein bohat chhota hai, is liye C − x ≈ C:
Ka ≈ x²/C
Square root lene se: x ≈ √(Ka × C)
Lehaza [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C)

Misaal: 0.1 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵) ke liye [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(1.8 × 10⁻⁶) = 1.34 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³.

book_ref.quote: The expression for the acid dissociation constant (Ka) is:

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein doosra denominator "C –" chhapa hai; durust C – x hai. Sample Problem 9.3 mein 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ × 0.1 = 1.8 × 10⁻⁶ hai, 0.18 × 10⁻⁶ nahi.

blocks.prompt:
11 Calculate [H₃O⁺], the pH and the percentage dissociation of a 0.20 mol dm⁻³ solution of acetic acid. (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵) (4 marks)
(0.20 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid solution ki [H₃O⁺], pH aur percentage dissociation nikalein. (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵))
blocks.explanation: Acetic acid weak hai, is liye [H₃O⁺] ≈ √(Ka × C); phir pH = −log[H₃O⁺] aur % dissociation = ([H₃O⁺]/C) × 100.

book_ref.quote: Calculate the concentration of [H₃O⁺] in a 0.1 M (mol dm⁻³) solution of acetic acid [CH₃COOH]

steps: CH₃COOH + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺; C = 0.20 mol dm⁻³

blocks.prompt:
12 A 0.050 mol dm⁻³ solution of a weak monobasic acid HA has pH = 3.15. Calculate the Ka of the acid and classify it. (4 marks)
(Aik weak monobasic acid HA ke 0.050 mol dm⁻³ solution ka pH = 3.15 hai. Acid ka Ka nikalein aur us ki darja bandi karein.)
blocks.explanation: pH se [H₃O⁺] = [A⁻] nikalein; bacha hua acid C − [H₃O⁺]; yeh qeematein Ka = [H₃O⁺][A⁻]/[HA] mein rakhein.

book_ref.quote: This equation can be used to calculate Ka for any acidic solution if we know the pH or [H⁺] of that solution

steps: Ka < 10⁻³, is liye HA weak acid hai

blocks.prompt:
13 Define the common ion effect. Explain it with the purification of sodium chloride by passing HCl gas through brine, giving the equilibrium equations. (4 marks)
(Common ion effect ki definition likhein. Brine mein HCl gas guzaar kar sodium chloride saaf karne ki misaal se equilibrium equations ke saath is ki wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Common ion effect: weak electrolyte mein common ion dal kar us ki ionization ko dabana.

NaCl ki safai: brine NaCl ka saturated solution hai jis mein NaCl poori tarah ionized hai:
NaCl(s) ⇌ Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
Kc = [Na⁺][Cl⁻] / [NaCl]

HCl gas bhi solution mein ionize hoti hai:
HCl(g) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)

Cl⁻ common ion hai. HCl gas guzarne se Cl⁻ ki concentration barhti hai. Equilibrium constant ki qeemat qaim rakhne ke liye Na⁺ aur Cl⁻ mil kar NaCl ke crystals banate hain:
Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) → NaCl(s)

Aam nateeja: kam hal hone wale electrolyte ke solution mein common ion dalne se us ki ionization dab jati hai; unionized species ki concentration barhti hai aur yeh precipitate ban kar nikal sakti hai.

book_ref.quote: This type of effect is called the common ion effect.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein HCl ke saath "(g)(s)" chhapa hai; HCl yahan gas hai: HCl(g) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).

blocks.prompt:
14 Explain with equations how the common ion effect is used in salt analysis (i) to obtain a low concentration of S²⁻ ions for the second group basic radicals (ii) to control [OH⁻] in the group reagent for the third group basic radicals. (4 marks)
(Equations ke saath wazahat karein ke salt analysis mein common ion effect kaise istemal hota hai (i) doosre group ke basic radicals ke liye S²⁻ ions ki kam concentration hasil karne mein (ii) teesre group ke basic radicals ke group reagent mein [OH⁻] ko qaboo karne mein.)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Doosra group: H₂S weak acid hai:
H₂S(g) ⇌ 2H⁺(aq) + S²⁻(aq)
Zyada strong acid HCl dala jata hai: HCl(aq) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
H⁺ common ion hai. Yeh H₂S ki dissociation dabata hai, aur acidic solution mein H₂S kam dissociate hota hai. Is tarah S²⁻ ions ki kam concentration banti hai jo salt analysis mein doosre group ke basic radicals ko precipitate karne mein madad deti hai.

(ii) Teesra group: NH₃ solution OH⁻ deta hai:
NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
NH₄Cl dala jata hai; yeh strong electrolyte hai: NH₄Cl(aq) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
Common ion NH₄⁺ ki bari miqdaar NH₃ solution ki ionization dabati hai, is liye OH⁻ ki concentration kam ho jati hai. NH₄Cl + NH₃ (NH₄OH) ka mel teesre group ke basic radicals ka group reagent hai.

Is tarah common ion effect qualitative analysis (aur buffers banane) mein wasee tor par istemal hota hai.

book_ref.quote: This low concentration of S²⁻ ions helps to do the precipitation of radicals

blocks.prompt:
15 What are buffer solutions? How are acidic and basic buffers prepared? Explain how an acetic acid-sodium acetate buffer resists a change in pH. (4 marks)
(Buffer solutions kya hain? Acidic aur basic buffers kaise banaye jate hain? Wazahat karein ke acetic acid-sodium acetate buffer pH ki tabdeeli ko kaise rokta hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Buffer solutions: woh solutions jo thora acid ya base dalne par apne pH ki tabdeeli ko rokte hain. In ka pH muqarrar hota hai jo patla karne ya der tak rakhne se nahi badalta.

Tayyari:
1. Acidic buffer (pH < 7): weak acid + strong base ke saath us ka salt, maslan CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa.
2. Basic buffer (pH > 7): weak base + strong acid ke saath us ka salt, maslan NH₄OH + NH₄Cl.

Acetic acid-sodium acetate buffer ka amal:
CH₃COOH(aq) + H₂O(ℓ) ⇌ CH₃COO⁻(aq) + H₃O⁺(aq)
CH₃COONa(aq) → CH₃COO⁻(aq) + Na⁺(aq)
CH₃COOH weak electrolyte hai; CH₃COONa strong electrolyte hai jis ka CH₃COO⁻ CH₃COOH ki dissociation dabata hai (common ion effect). Is liye buffer CH₃COOH aur CH₃COO⁻ ka bara zakheera hai.

Acid dalne par: shamil H₃O⁺ CH₃COO⁻ se mil kar wapas acetic acid banata hai, jo weak acid hone ki wajah se undissociated rehta hai:
CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺ → CH₃COOH + H₂O
Is liye pH taqreeban wahi rehta hai.

Base dalne par: shamil OH⁻ acid se react karta hai: CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O, aur pH phir taqreeban wahi rehta hai. NH₄Cl-NH₄OH buffer bhi isi tarah pH aur pOH ki tabdeeli rokta hai.

book_ref.quote: Buffer solutions are mostly prepared by mixing two substances.

blocks.prompt:
16 Write Henderson's equation for the pH of an acidic buffer. Which factors govern the pH of a buffer? Show that the best buffer has pH = pKa, and use Table 9.4 to explain the effect of adding acetate ions to acetic acid. (4 marks)
(Acidic buffer ke pH ke liye Henderson ki equation likhein. Buffer ka pH kin factors par munhasir hai? Dikhayein ke sab se achhe buffer ka pH = pKa hai, aur Table 9.4 se acetic acid mein acetate ions dalne ka asar samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Weak acid HA aur us ke salt NaA ka buffer:
HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻;  NaA ⇌ Na⁺ + A⁻

Henderson ki equation:
pH = pKa − log([Acid]/[Salt])
Numerator aur denominator badalne se log ka nishan badalta hai:
pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid])

Factors: (i) istemal hone wale acid ka pKa; (ii) salt aur acid ki concentrations ki nisbat.

Sab se achha buffer: salt aur acid ki barabar concentrations se. Acetic acid-sodium acetate ke liye [CH₃COOH] = [CH₃COONa]:
pH = pKa + log(1) = pKa + 0 = pKa = 4.74
Yani aise buffer ka pH acid ke pKa ke barabar hai.

Table 9.4 (0.10 mol dm⁻³ CH₃COOH): [CH₃COO⁻] 0.00 → 0.05 → 0.10 → 0.15 mol dm⁻³ hone par % dissociation 1.3 → 0.036 → 0.018 → 0.012 girti hai aur pH 2.89 → 4.44 → 4.74 → 4.92 barhta hai. Acetate acetic acid ki dissociation dabata hai; [CH₃COOH] jitna [CH₃COONa] se zyada, pH utna kam.

book_ref.quote: This equation shows that two factors evidently govern the pH of a buffer solution.

blocks.prompt:
17 A buffer is prepared with 0.25 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid and 0.10 mol dm⁻³ sodium acetate. Calculate its pH (pKa of acetic acid = 4.74). Is it an acidic or a basic buffer? (4 marks)
(0.25 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid aur 0.10 mol dm⁻³ sodium acetate se buffer banaya gaya. Is ka pH nikalein (acetic acid ka pKa = 4.74). Yeh acidic buffer hai ya basic?)
blocks.explanation: Salt aur acid ki concentrations Henderson ki equation pH = pKa + log([Salt]/[Acid]) mein rakhein.

book_ref.quote: pH of a buffer solution can be calculated by using Henderson equation as given below:

steps: pH < 7: acidic buffer (weak acid + strong base ke saath us ka salt)

blocks.prompt:
18 How many moles of sodium acetate must be dissolved in 1.0 dm³ of 0.10 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid to obtain a buffer of pH 5.04? (pKa = 4.74; assume no change in volume) (4 marks)
(1.0 dm³ 0.10 mol dm⁻³ acetic acid mein sodium acetate ke kitne moles hal kiye jayen ke pH 5.04 ka buffer bane? (pKa = 4.74; volume mein tabdeeli nahi))
blocks.explanation: Henderson ki equation se [Salt]/[Acid] ki nisbat nikalein, phir [Acid] aur volume se zarb dein.

book_ref.quote: So, pH is controlled by pKa of the acid.

steps: CH₃COONa ke moles = 0.20 mol dm⁻³ × 1.0 dm³ = 0.20 mol

blocks.prompt:
19 What is the solubility product? Derive the Ksp expression for PbSO₄, write it for PbCl₂, and state the general rule for writing Ksp. Use Table 9.6 to relate Ksp to solubility. (4 marks)
(Solubility product kya hai? PbSO₄ ke Ksp ka expression nikalein, PbCl₂ ke liye likhein, aur Ksp likhne ka aam usool bayan karein. Table 9.6 se Ksp ka solubility se taaluq batayein.)
blocks.explanation:
NaCl jaisa zyada hal hone wala ionic compound poori tarah dissociate hota hai, magar kam hal hone wale salt ki dissociation equilibrium par poori nahi hoti. Jab PbSO₄ ko paani ke saath hilaya jaye to solution mein Pb²⁺, SO₄²⁻ aur undissociated PbSO₄ hote hain; thos aur hal shuda ions ke darmiyan equilibrium hota hai:
PbSO₄(s) ⇌ Pb²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq)
Kc = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻] / [PbSO₄]

Bohat kam hal hone ki wajah se PbSO₄ ki concentration taqreeban constant hai, is liye ise Kc ke saath le jate hain:
Kc[PbSO₄] = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻]
Kc[PbSO₄] = Ksp, is liye Ksp = [Pb²⁺][SO₄²⁻] = 25 °C par 1.6 × 10⁻⁸

PbCl₂ ke liye (PbCl₂ ⇌ Pb²⁺ + 2Cl⁻): Ksp = [Pb²⁺][Cl⁻]²

Definition: solubility product ions ki concentrations ka hasil-e-zarb hai, har aik ko balanced equation ke coefficient ki power de kar. Ksp aam tor par kamre ke temperature par bohat chhota hota hai, temperature par munhasir hai, aur kam hal hone wale salt ki dissociation ka paimana hai.

Solubility se taaluq (molar solubility S): 2-ion wale salt jaise PbSO₄ ke liye Ksp = S² (S = 1.3 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³); 3-ion wale salts jaise Ca(OH)₂ ya CaF₂ ke liye Ksp = S(2S)² = 4S³ (Ca(OH)₂: 6.5 × 10⁻⁶, S = 1.175 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³; CaF₂: 3.2 × 10⁻¹¹, S = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³).

book_ref.quote: It means that equilibrium exists between solid solute, PbSO₄ and the dissolved ions

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein dissolved ions "SO₄²⁻ and SO₄²⁻" chhape hain (durust: Pb²⁺ aur SO₄²⁻), aur Table 9.6 mein PbSO₄ ka Ksp 1.69 × 10⁻⁴ chhapa hai (durust: 1.6 × 10⁻⁸). Table 9.6 ki solubilities mol dm⁻³ mein hain.

blocks.prompt:
20 Explain how the solubility product is used to predict precipitation, illustrating with the CaSO₄ example. How does a common ion affect the solubility of a sparingly soluble salt? (4 marks)
(Wazahat karein ke solubility product se precipitate banne ki pesh goi kaise hoti hai, CaSO₄ ki misaal ke saath. Common ion kam hal hone wale salt ki solubility par kya asar daalta hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Precipitate ki pesh goi: maujood ions ki concentrations ka hasil-e-zarb (ionic product) Ksp se milaya jata hai:

Misaal: CaSO₄ ka Ksp = 2 × 10⁻⁵. 25 °C par Ca²⁺ ka 10⁻² mol dm⁻³ solution SO₄²⁻ ke 10⁻² mol dm⁻³ solution mein milaya gaya. Milane ke baad (barabar volumes):
[Ca²⁺] = [SO₄²⁻] = 10⁻²/2 = 5.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³
Ionic product = (5.0 × 10⁻³)(5.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol² dm⁻⁶
2.5 × 10⁻⁵ > 2 × 10⁻⁵ (Ksp), is liye CaSO₄ precipitate hota hai.

Common ion ka solubility par asar: common ion ki maujoodgi kam hal hone wale ionic compound ki solubility kam karti hai. PbCrO₄ ke saturated solution (PbCrO₄ ⇌ Pb²⁺ + CrO₄²⁻) mein CrO₄²⁻ dene wala hal pazeer salt dalne se CrO₄²⁻ Pb²⁺ se mil kar mazeed PbCrO₄ banata hai; Ksp qaim rakhne ke liye equilibrium baayen taraf jata hai, aur kam PbCrO₄ hal rehta hai.

book_ref.quote: The solubility product can also help in predicting whether the precipitation of a salt will occur or not.

blocks.prompt:
21 The solubility product of PbCl₂ at a certain temperature is 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ (value given). Calculate its molar solubility and the concentrations of Pb²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in its saturated solution. (4 marks)
(Kisi temperature par PbCl₂ ka solubility product 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ hai (qeemat di gayi). Is ki molar solubility aur saturated solution mein Pb²⁺ aur Cl⁻ ions ki concentrations nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Molar solubility S farz karein; har PbCl₂ aik Pb²⁺ aur do Cl⁻ deta hai, is liye Ksp = S(2S)² = 4S³.

book_ref.quote: Similarly, for another sparingly soluble salt, PbCl₂.

blocks.final_answer: S = 1.62 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³; [Pb²⁺] = 1.62 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³, [Cl⁻] = 3.24 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³

blocks.prompt:
22 At a certain temperature the molar solubility of Ca(OH)₂ is 1.05 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³. Calculate [Ca²⁺], [OH⁻] and the Ksp of Ca(OH)₂ at this temperature. (4 marks)
(Kisi temperature par Ca(OH)₂ ki molar solubility 1.05 × 10⁻² mol dm⁻³ hai. Is temperature par [Ca²⁺], [OH⁻] aur Ca(OH)₂ ka Ksp nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Har Ca(OH)₂ aik Ca²⁺ aur do OH⁻ deta hai; S aur 2S ko Ksp = [Ca²⁺][OH⁻]² mein rakhein.

book_ref.quote: The concentration of OH⁻ is double than the concentration of Ca²⁺

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book ke sample problem mein equilibrium stage par "S + S" chhapa hai; durust S aur 2S hai, kyun ke har Ca(OH)₂ do OH⁻ deta hai.

blocks.prompt:
23 Predict whether a precipitate forms in each case (equal volumes are mixed): (i) a solution with 4.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ Pb²⁺ ions and a solution with 2.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ SO₄²⁻ ions (Ksp of PbSO₄ = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸) (ii) a solution with 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ Ag⁺ ions and a solution with 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ Cl⁻ ions (Ksp of AgCl = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰). (4 marks)
(Har soorat mein batayein ke precipitate banega ya nahi (barabar volumes milaye gaye): (i) 4.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ Pb²⁺ ions wala solution aur 2.0 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ SO₄²⁻ ions wala solution (PbSO₄ ka Ksp = 1.6 × 10⁻⁸) (ii) 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ Ag⁺ ions wala solution aur 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ Cl⁻ ions wala solution (AgCl ka Ksp = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰).)
blocks.explanation: Barabar volumes milane se har concentration aadhi ho jati hai; mixture ka ionic product Ksp se milayein.

book_ref.quote: As the product of concentrations is greater than Ksp, therefore CaSO₄ will precipitate out.

steps: Ionic product = (2.0 × 10⁻³)(1.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ mol² dm⁻⁶ > 1.6 × 10⁻⁸, is liye PbSO₄ precipitate hota hai
Ionic product = (1.0 × 10⁻⁵)(1.0 × 10⁻⁵) = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol² dm⁻⁶ < 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰, is liye solution unsaturated hai: precipitate nahi
blocks.final_answer: (i) PbSO₄ precipitate hota hai (2.0 × 10⁻⁶ > Ksp); (ii) AgCl ka precipitate nahi (1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ < Ksp)

blocks.prompt:
24 What is salt hydrolysis? Explain, with equations, the nature of aqueous solutions of the salts of (i) a strong acid and strong base (ii) a strong acid and weak base (iii) a weak acid and strong base (iv) a weak acid and weak base. (4 marks)
(Salt hydrolysis kya hai? Equations ke saath in salts ke aqueous solutions ki nauiyat samjhayein: (i) strong acid aur strong base (ii) strong acid aur weak base (iii) weak acid aur strong base (iv) weak acid aur weak base.)
blocks.explanation:
Salt hydrolysis: salt paani mein hal ho kar apne ions mein toot-ta hai; yeh ions paani se react kar ke pH badal sakte hain, is baat par munhasir ke salt kis acid aur base se bana hai.

(i) Strong acid + strong base, maslan NaCl:
NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
Cl⁻ (strong HCl ka conjugate base) aur Na⁺ (strong NaOH ka conjugate acid) bohat weak hain aur paani se khaas react nahi karte. Solution neutral rehta hai.

(ii) Strong acid + weak base, maslan NH₄Cl:
NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
NH₄⁺(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₃ + H₃O⁺(aq)
NH₄⁺ (weak NH₃ ka conjugate acid) H₃O⁺ banata hai; Cl⁻ react nahi karta. Solution acidic hai.

(iii) Weak acid + strong base, maslan CH₃COONa:
CH₃COO⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ CH₃COOH(aq) + OH⁻(aq)
CH₃COO⁻ (weak CH₃COOH ka conjugate base) OH⁻ banata hai; Na⁺ pH par asar nahi daalta. Solution basic hai.

(iv) Weak acid + weak base, maslan NH₄CH₃COO:
NH₄CH₃COO(aq) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + CH₃COO⁻(aq)
NH₄⁺ + H₂O ⇌ NH₃ + H₃O⁺ aur CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻
Dono ions hydrolyze hote hain; pH un ki nisbati taqat par munhasir hai. Solution acidic, basic ya taqreeban neutral ho sakta hai, is par munhasir ke kaun sa reaction ghalib hai.

book_ref.quote: When a salt dissolves in water, it dissociates into its constituent ions.

header: Paani se react karne wala ion

blocks.prompt:
25 What is an acid-base indicator? Explain the working of a weak-acid indicator HIn in acidic and basic solutions. State the criteria for selecting an indicator for a titration. (4 marks)
(Acid-base indicator kya hai? Acidic aur basic solutions mein weak-acid indicator HIn ka amal samjhayein. Titration ke liye indicator chunne ki sharait bayan karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Indicator: woh substance jo rang badal kar titration ka end point zahir karti hai. Acid-base indicators acid mein aik rang aur base mein doosra rang dikhate hain; zyada tar weak organic acids ya weak organic bases hote hain.

Weak-acid indicator: HIn ⇌ H⁺ + In⁻
In⁻ indicator ka anion hissa hai. Reaction reversible hai, is liye HIn aur In⁻ dono maujood hote hain; rang is liye nazar aate hain ke HIn aur In⁻ ke rang alag hain.

Acidic solution mein: In⁻ ions Bronsted bases ban kar acid se proton lete hain. Indicator zyada tar unionized HIn hota hai aur acid wala rang dikhata hai.

Basic solution mein: base ke OH⁻ ions indicator ke H⁺ ions se mil jate hain. H⁺ ki kami poori karne ke liye indicator molecules mazeed ionize hote hain, is liye indicator zyada tar In⁻ hota hai aur base wala rang dikhata hai (litmus ke liye neela).

Indicator range: rang kisi pH par HIn aur In⁻ ki nisbati miqdaar par munhasir hai; indicator taqreeban 2 pH units mein rang badalta hai. Methyl red pH 4.4 aur 6.2 ke darmiyan laal se peela hota hai (pH 4.4 par zyada tar laal HIn).

Chunne ki sharait:
1. Titration ke aakhir ka pH indicator ke neutral point (rang badalne ki range) ke qareeb ho.
2. Indicator equivalence point ke qareeb tez rang ki tabdeeli dikhaye.

book_ref.quote: Acid-base indicators exhibit one color in acid and another in base.

blocks.prompt:
26 Describe the titration curve for the titration of aqueous ammonia with hydrochloric acid. Why is the pH at the equivalence point below 7, and which indicator is suitable? (4 marks)
(Aqueous ammonia ki hydrochloric acid se titration ka titration curve bayan karein. Equivalence point par pH 7 se kam kyun hota hai aur kaun sa indicator munasib hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Shuru: solution mein sirf weak base NH₃ hota hai jo thora sa dissociate hota hai aur strong base se kam [OH⁻] deta hai. Shuru ka pH 7 se zyada magar strong base se kam hota hai.

HCl dalna: HCl dalne se [OH⁻] kam hoti hai aur pH mazeed girta hai.

Equivalence point se pehle: solution buffer jaise hisse mein hota hai jahan pH ahista badalta hai. Weak base aur us ka conjugate acid NH₄⁺ (banne wale salt se) buffer jaisa asar paida karte hain jo acid dalne par pH ki tabdeeli ko narm karta hai.

Equivalence point: pH 7 se kam (pH = 5.27) hota hai, kyun ke conjugate acid thora sa dissociate ho kar H⁺ deta hai aur solution acidic ho jata hai:
NH₄⁺ → NH₃ + H⁺

Equivalence point ke baad: pH tezi se girta hai, kyun ke zaid strong acid poori tarah dissociate ho kar zyada [H⁺] deta hai.

Indicator: methyl orange (acid mein laal, base mein peela, range 3.2-4.5) isi acidic range mein rang badalta hai, is liye strong acid-weak base titrations mein istemal hota hai (Table 9.7).

book_ref.quote: Initially, the solution contains only the weak base and it only partially dissociates

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein likha hai ke buffering "base dalne par" pH ki tabdeeli narm karti hai; yahan acid (HCl) dala ja raha hai, is liye durust "acid dalne par" hai. Methyl orange acid mein laal hota hai, orange nahi.

blocks.prompt:
27 Define the equivalence point and the end point of a titration. How does a titration curve help in choosing an indicator? Illustrate with the strong acid-strong base titration and Table 9.7. (4 marks)
(Titration ke equivalence point aur end point ki definition likhein. Titration curve indicator chunne mein kaise madad karta hai? Strong acid-strong base titration aur Table 9.7 se wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation:
pH curve: solution ke pH ka shamil titrant ke volume ke muqable mein graph; yeh dikhata hai ke acidic ya basic solution mein base ya acid dalne par pH kaise badalta hai.

Equivalence point: woh point jahan shamil titrant analyte solution ko poori tarah neutral karne ke liye bilkul kaafi ho.
End point: woh point jahan indicator rang badalta hai.

Indicator chunna: titration curve dikhata hai ke pH ki tez tabdeeli (equivalence point) kahan hai. Aisa indicator chuna jata hai jis ka end point (rang badalne ki range) equivalence point ke qareeb ho.

Strong acid-strong base (HCl aur NaOH): shuru mein sirf strong acid hota hai jo poori tarah dissociate hota hai, is liye [H⁺] zyada aur pH bohat kam hota hai. NaOH dalne se OH⁻ H⁺ ko neutral karta hai aur pH barhta hai. Equivalence point tab aata hai jab shamil OH⁻ shuru ke H⁺ ke stoichiometric barabar ho; wahan pH 7.0 hai. Curve mein pH taqreeban 4.0 se 10.0 tak tezi se barhta hai, is liye phenolphthalein, jo is range mein rang badalta hai, istemal ho sakta hai.

Table 9.7:
Methyl orange: acid mein laal, base mein peela, range 3.2-4.5; strong acid-strong base aur strong acid-weak base titrations.
Phenolphthalein: acid mein berang, base mein laal, range 8.2-10.0; weak acid-strong base titrations.

book_ref.quote: We can use the titration curve to choose an indicator that will show when the titration is complete
